name: Output ownership and patent invalidity
blurb: Protection against third party claims that generated output infringes an existing patent.
summary: Protection against third party claims that generated output infringes an existing patent.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: A blanket exclusion for patent infringement in the base commercial general liability policy, which would leave the AI output exposure completely uncovered unless a separate IP policy is purchased.
An intellectual property exclusion in a cyber or media liability policy that carves out patent claims while covering only copyright and trademark, leaving the most severe exposure uninsured.
A known or anticipated claims exclusion that bars coverage if the insured had any pre-policy awareness of a specific patent or a cease and desist letter related to the AI output.
A willful infringement exclusion that eliminates coverage for enhanced damages, which are common in patent cases where the insured continued selling AI output after learning of the patent.

A sublimit for intellectual property claims that is far below the potential exposure, such as a one million dollar sublimit on a policy with a ten million dollar general limit, which would be quickly exhausted by patent litigation.

An exclusion for declaratory judgment or patent invalidity actions, meaning the insurer will not pay defense costs when a patent holder seeks a ruling of infringement without initially demanding damages.
A prior acts exclusion or retroactive date that is set after the AI model was first deployed, cutting off coverage for any output generated before that date even if the claim arises later.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete the standard patent infringement exclusion from the commercial general liability policy and replace it with a specific grant of coverage for patent infringement arising from AI generated output.
Add an endorsement defining AI generated output as your product or your work so that the policy's products and completed operations coverage responds to downstream patent claims.
Include coverage for induced and contributory patent infringement, not just direct infringement, because AI output often becomes a component in a customer's larger product.
Add a declaratory judgment and patent invalidity defense cost endorsement so the insurer pays legal fees when a patent holder seeks a non monetary ruling of infringement.
Negotiate a willful infringement carve back that covers enhanced damages up to the policy limit, provided the insured did not deliberately copy a known patented invention.
Add a worldwide territory endorsement with a schedule of covered jurisdictions, removing any limitation to the United States or named countries where the AI output is sold.
Include a contractual liability endorsement covering the insured's indemnity obligations to customers for patent infringement caused by AI output, subject to the same policy terms and limits.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption from a patent injunction is not typically covered under a liability policy, but a manuscript endorsement can add a waiting period of thirty to sixty days before loss of profits from an injunction is payable, subject to a separate sublimit.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Coverage for loss of profits due to a preliminary or permanent injunction stopping sales of AI output is available only by endorsement, usually with a sublimit of one to five million dollars and a requirement that the injunction be based on a covered patent infringement claim.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: No property or equipment breakdown coverage is relevant to patent infringement claims arising from AI output, so this line is not placed as part of this program.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: The liability program is structured with a primary IP policy providing a per claim limit typically between five and ten million dollars, with first and second excess layers each adding ten to twenty five million dollars in capacity depending on the insured's revenue and patent exposure.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A standard commercial general liability policy typically excludes patent infringement entirely, so the primary layer must be a specialized intellectual property or technology errors and omissions policy with patent infringement coverage.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made basis applies because patent infringement claims often surface years after the AI output was first generated or sold, and the continuous nature of AI output distribution makes occurrence triggers impractical.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess layers follow form over the primary IP policy and provide additional limits in a tower, with each layer attaching only after the underlying limits are exhausted by payment of covered claims.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Direct patent infringement claims alleging that the AI generated output itself, when made, used, sold, or imported, falls within the claims of an existing patent.
Induced infringement claims alleging that the insured actively encouraged customers or users to employ the AI output in a manner that infringes a third party patent.
Contributory infringement claims alleging that the AI output is a material component of a larger product or process with no substantial non infringing use.
Willful infringement allegations that could lead to enhanced damages up to treble the actual damages if the insured had knowledge of the patent and continued to distribute the output.
Downstream customer claims for breach of warranty or indemnity when those customers are sued for patent infringement due to incorporating the AI output into their own products.
Cross border exposure where the same AI output infringes different patents in multiple jurisdictions, multiplying defense costs and potential damages.
Declaratory judgment actions by patent holders seeking a ruling that the AI output infringes, which can force the insured into costly litigation even without a direct damages claim.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What type of AI system generates the output and does it have the capacity to create novel technical solutions, designs, or processes that could embody patented subject matter?
Has the insured conducted any freedom to operate searches or patent clearance reviews on representative AI outputs before commercial release?
What contractual indemnities does the insured provide to customers or downstream users for patent infringement arising from AI generated output?
In which jurisdictions does the insured sell or distribute AI generated output, given that patent rights are territorial and infringement exposure varies by country?
Does the AI training data or model incorporate any third party patented algorithms, methods, or components that could taint the output?
What is the volume and revenue associated with AI generated output, and what is the largest single contract or customer concentration?
Has the insured received any cease and desist letters, licensing demands, or patent infringement claims related to AI output in the past five years?
